claims.text: The proposed material is a bulk, homogenized, equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi exhibits superior elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance compared with conventional steels.
The composition of AlCoCrFeNi drives the formation of stable protective oxide layers.
Enhanced microstructural stability contributes to the alloy's superior tribo-corrosion resistance.
A stable, protective oxide scale forms on AlCoCrFeNi under elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
The multi-principal-element configuration of AlCoCrFeNi promotes slower diffusion kinetics.
Slower diffusion kinetics enable the formation of robust protective surface oxides.
The protective surface oxides reduce material loss caused by combined wear and corrosion.
AlCoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower mass-loss rate than conventional stainless steel under identical tribo-corrosion conditions.
AlCoCrFeNi will sustain significantly less surface damage than conventional stainless steel under identical tribo-corrosion conditions.
Common stainless steels or Ni-based superalloys exhibit moderate to high wear and corrosion under elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
The proposed benefit is expected at moderate to high temperatures up to 800 °C when all principal elements remain within an appropriate compositional range.
Temperatures beyond the proposed range or large compositional deviations could impair oxide stability and overall performance.
